summary: A table preview (an archive's listing, or a file opened through Nushell) scrolls down to its last row, and still scrolls sideways. In the table arm of `preview_body` (src/finder/preview.rs) the element that `.overflow_scrollbar()` wraps has `.self_start()`. The kit's wrapper for both directions lays its scroll area out as a flex row with the wrapped element as its one item (gpui-component-0.8.1/src/scroll/scrollable.rs). The row stretched that item to the area's height with the table spilling out of it, and GPUI measures how far an area scrolls from the area's direct children (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs, prepaint), so nothing overflowed downward. Aligned to the start, the item is as tall as the table, or as the area (the kit's min-height of 100%) for a shorter table. The kit copies align_self to its outer wrapper too, where it does nothing, because that wrapper is 100% wide. The line under the table is observed as `preview-table-footer` for the tests. The same arm draws in the Preview Pane, the column view's card, the gallery, Quick Look's window and Quick Look's dialog in --term mode; each has a test and pictures.
changelog: A table preview scrolls down. The preview of a zip or tar archive, and of a database or another file opened with Nushell, showed only the rows that fit in its space, such as the first eight of an archive's items in the Preview Pane, and the others couldn't be reached, while the line under the table counted them all. The table now scrolls down to its last row in the gallery, the column view, the Preview Pane, and Quick Look, and still scrolls sideways when it is wider than its space. In the column view, the wheel over such a table scrolls the table, where it used to move the columns sideways.
behaviour_changes: A table preview with more rows than fit scrolls down with the wheel or the trackpad, to its last row, which then ends right above the line with the count. Tested and seen in pictures in the Preview Pane beside the list, the column view's card, the gallery, Quick Look's window and Quick Look's dialog in --term mode. Seen for zip archives of 150, 60 (long names, cut with an ellipsis) and 260 items (200 listed, "The first 200 items"), a .tar.gz of 90, a SQLite database's 40 tables through Nushell, and a table of 12 columns and 200 rows (a CSV that Nushell opens because a NUL byte keeps it from being text).
The heading row is part of what scrolls: it goes out of view with the first rows. Scrolled sideways it stays over its columns.

A vertical scrollbar thumb shows while such a table scrolls and can be dragged (probe: 60 points of drag moved the table 1295). Where the table is also wider than its space both thumbs show while scrolling. That is the usual case in the Preview Pane at its default width and in the column view's card, where a two-column table (300 points at least) is 55 and 30 points wider than its space: the horizontal thumb appears over the bottom visible row while scrolling down and fades. Before, it showed only on a sideways scroll.

Column view: the wheel over a table with rows out of view scrolls the table. Before, it moved the columns sideways when they were wider than the window. At the table's top and bottom the table keeps the wheel, as the kit has every scroll area do and as a long text preview in the card does (its bottom is now in a test). A table that shows all its rows leaves the wheel to the columns, as before.
A table that is too long by less than a row scrolls by what was cut: an archive of 8 items in the Preview Pane had its eighth row cut by 8.5 points and now scrolls that far.

Sideways scrolling is unchanged, and down, sideways and down again works in one table (test). A packet with both directions in it goes the way it mostly points: (-30, -50) moved the table 50 down and not sideways, (-30, -10) moved it 30 sideways (probe). A mouse wheel that reports lines works too: 5 lines moved the table 130 points.

Each file still starts at its top and left edge, another file is not left where the last one was scrolled to, and a text size change in Quick Look keeps the place (tests). Closing and opening the pane, or going to another file and back, starts the table at its top, as with the other previews (probe).
With the table scrolled to its end, a window made shorter leaves the table where it is, with rows below again to scroll to, and a window made taller keeps the last row at the bottom (probe).

A table at rest looks exactly as before: 18 pictures of tables at rest, or after a wheel turn that has nowhere to go, are pixel-identical between the trunk's source and the change, in all five surfaces, for long, short and 12-column tables and a 520-point pane. A table that fits ignores the wheel as before: in a probe of 990 tables (scale factors 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2; the pane, the gallery and Quick Look; text of 8 to 32 points; 1 to 60 rows) none that fits moved at all, and every one that doesn't moved exactly as far as it overflows, to its last row and back.

On a Mac the kit's wrapper lets what it scrolls bounce at its ends, and a table now does, like the other previews. No Mac was at hand; see the notes for the same code run on Linux with the bounce turned on.
Not visible: element ID `preview-table-footer` on the line under the table.

docs/manual.md, the Previews table: the archive row says that a table with more rows than fit scrolls down and one wider than its space scrolls sideways; the Nushell row says that it scrolls like an archive's table.
left_out: The heading row is not kept in view. It scrolls away with the first rows, as it would with the brief's first way out. For an archive (Name, Size) nothing is lost; in a table of many columns from Nushell the columns have no names once it is scrolled down, and explore mode, which has a fixed heading, is the way to read such data. Keeping it needs a scroll area built by hand around a heading and a body that share a handle, as explore mode has.

The rows are not drawn with a uniform list. Every row and cell is still built and laid out on each frame the preview draws, as before; the cap is 200 rows, the columns have none. Measured in a debug build on the loaded machine, in the gallery: a frame with a 151-row archive takes 8 ms and with 12 columns by 200 rows 22 to 33 ms, against 5.5 ms with a text file, the same with and without the change, and the same for a wheel step with its frame. The change adds no element. A table of very many columns was slow to redraw before and still is.

Neither of the brief's two ways out was taken. The implementer's third one keeps the kit's wrapper and stops its row from stretching the wrapped element. It keeps both scrollbars, the wrapper's per-file ID, the bounce on a Mac and the look at rest, in one line. I agree with it. It leans on two things inside gpui-component 0.8.1 (the both-axes scroll area is a flex row, and the element keeps its align_self as the area's content); if a kit update changes either, the five tests fail rather than the bug coming back silently.

No committed test for a wheel that reports lines, for dragging the scrollbar's thumb, or for the bounce; all three were probed. No committed test with a table from Nushell: the arm is the same for it, and the pictures have a database and a 12-column table.

examples/screenshot.rs still has no step that turns the wheel. The pictures used the implementer's temporary one, which is not committed: /home/user/polish-tools/shots/table-preview-scroll-add-scroll-steps.py (scroll:x,y,dy[,dx], qlscroll:, qlkey:, qlclick:, and SHOT_TERM=1 for --term mode). It applied to the trunk's example unchanged.
Nothing was built or run on macOS or Windows. The change has no platform-specific code.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature changed.
README.md states nothing that changed, the Search Syntax dialog is not affected, and CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide says; the entry is in the commit message.

review_fixes: a_table_in_the_column_views_card_takes_the_wheel_only_when_it_scrolls now also turns the wheel far past the table's end in the column view's card and asserts that the last row ends at the line with the count and that the columns have not moved. The changelog names the column view among the places where the table scrolls to its last row, and the commit message says a table keeps the wheel at its ends; neither was pinned there (the other four surfaces had their end checked). The test's comment says so too. It fails without the change at the same assertion as before, the first one.

The comment on `.self_start()` said that without it there is nothing below the area to scroll down to. The table does spill below the area; what counts is that an area scrolls no further than its own children reach, and the stretched element ends at the area's edge. The comment now says that.

Commit message. The paragraph on the Mac said the bounce could not be run. It now says what was run: the same code on Linux with the bounce turned on (see the notes). The cause is worded as in the comment. The changelog paragraph gained a sentence on the column view, where the wheel over a long table used to move the columns: a change a user sees and the entry did not say.

notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 66d4fad: 616 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (614 one trunk commit earlier, before the rebase). `cargo check --lib -p fffinder`, the library as it ships without test-support, has no warnings. The five new tests pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42, 1234, 31337 and 99991 (run one trunk commit before the last rebase, which touched none of their files).

Tests fail without the change. With the whole src diff reverse-applied all five fail: four at their first "scrolled down" assertion and a_table_preview_scrolls_down_to_its_last_row earlier, at the missing preview-table-footer ID, which comes with the change. The proof that counts: with only the `.self_start()` line taken out, all five fail at the scroll (the pane: y 67 against -33; the narrow pane the same; the gallery 71 against -29; the column view's card (376, 67) against (436, 7), the columns having moved instead; the --term dialog 154 against 54). I ran that on the implementer's commit and again on the final test file. Quick Look's half of a_table_scrolls_down_in_the_gallery_and_in_quick_look is hidden behind the gallery's failure; the implementer ran it alone (y 1 against -99) and I did not repeat that.

Pictures. 44 pictures from the change and the same 44 from the source with the change reversed, in a folder of harder files of my own (table-preview-scroll-review-mkpics.py, -shots.sh, -pixdiff.py; nine sheets kept as table-preview-scroll-review-sheet-*.png). The 18 of a table at rest or after a wheel turn with nowhere to go are pixel-identical with the status bar masked. The 26 scrolled ones differ only inside the table's scroll area. They were taken before my two review edits, which change a comment and a test.

Probes, not kept in the repository (kept as table-preview-scroll-review-probes.rs beside the pictures). (1) Extents: see behaviour_changes, 990 tables. At scale factors that aren't whole, positions land on device pixels, so a wheel turn of 37 points moves a table 37.14 at 1.75 and 36.67 at 1.5; I allowed one device pixel there and none for a table that fits. (2) Frames: see left_out. (3) The Mac's bounce. The only thing in the kit's scroll path that differs on a Mac is that ScrollBounce is on by default (scroll_bounce.rs, enabled_by_default); the stretch and return are the same numbers as on Linux. So I put `.scroll_bounce(true)` on the table's and the text preview's wrappers, turned reduced motion off, and sent a trackpad's packets with their phases, a frame's time apart. In the pane, a table and a text preview gave the same numbers: 5 packets of 20 moved 100; momentum went on; pulled past the bottom the edge went 36 points out and no further, and came back to the end within about 40 frames with the last row 0 points from the count; a fling into the end went 33.5 out and back; the same at the top. A sideways swipe moved the table sideways (55, all there is in the pane) and the text not at all; a swipe mostly upward (4, 20) moved it 100 up and not sideways. In the column view's card a table that fits passed the swipe on to the columns, and a long one took it, bounced at its end and left the columns alone. (4) Odds and ends: a wheel in lines, a packet with both directions, the scrollbar's thumb, the wheel under the card and over the line with the count (nothing moves), another file and back, the pane and the window resized with the table at its end, the pane closed and opened.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code and the probes say. (1) A table that fits starts to take the wheel, or creeps by a fraction of a point, because the wrapped element comes out a hair taller than the area. Its height is the kit's min-height of 100% of the area, resolved by Taffy against the area's own height, both edges are snapped to device pixels from the same origin (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/taffy.rs, layout_bounds), and GPUI rounds the scroll range to two decimals (div.rs, clamp_scroll_position). The 990-table probe found none, at five scale factors. A table one row too long does scroll, by what was cut. (2) A table at rest is drawn differently somewhere, because the kit copies align_self to its outer wrapper as well (scrollable.rs, root_style_from). That wrapper is 100% wide in a column whose width is definite on every surface, so its alignment across the column changes nothing; the 18 identical pictures cover the five surfaces, short, long and wide tables, and a wide pane. (3) On a Mac, where the tests never run the bounce: the table stuck short of its end or displaced, a sideways swipe lost, or the wheel leaking to the columns in the middle of a gesture. See probe (3): the same code path, on Linux, behaves like a text preview's. What that can't show is a real trackpad's stream.

Doubts that remain. 1. Only Linux was built and run; the Mac's path was run on Linux as described, not on a Mac. 2. Two judgement calls of the implementer's that a user will see, both left as they are: the heading row scrolls away, and in the Preview Pane and the column view's card the horizontal thumb shows over the bottom row whenever an archive's table is scrolled down, because a two-column table is wider than those cards (see Found, not fixed). 3. In the column view the wheel over a long table no longer moves the columns. That is what a long text preview in the card has always done, and the wheel beside the table, on the details under the card, still moves them.

For briefs still to come.
- preview-page-keys: a table preview now has something to page through. If the cut step 4 (keys that scroll a preview) is taken up: the table scrolls in the kit's both-axes wrapper, `.self_start().overflow_scrollbar().id(("table-preview", path_id))`, whose ScrollHandle is the kit's own (window keyed state under that ID, inside the element path). An area built by hand to get at a handle must keep what `.self_start()` does: the element the area scrolls has to be the area's direct child and as tall as its content. In a flex row that means aligned to the start; in a column it comes by itself. `MatchScroll` in the same file is a worked example for one direction. The five tests above read `preview-table` (the heading and the rows, which moves with the scroll both ways) and `preview-table-footer` (the line under them, which doesn't); keep both.
- preview-card-height: a table in the card now scrolls down as well as sideways, inside the box. None of the new tests depends on the 240 points: the pane test wants a 151-row table (3724 points) to overflow by more than 1000; the column view test makes the window 560 by 600 and needs short.zip (three rows and the heading, about 98 points) to fit the box and long.zip not to; a_long_table_wider_than_the_pane_scrolls_both_ways drags the pane to its least width, which has to stay under the table's 300. Your `.flex_1().min_h_0()` box keeps the table arm's outer `v_flex().size_full()` at a definite height, which the kit's min-height of 100% inside it needs.
- stale-previews-and-cancel: a table preview replaced in place for the same path keeps its scroll position, now down as well as sideways, cut to the new table's size; a spinner frame in between starts it at its top.
- quick-look-empty-state, type-select-space: tests/term_mode.rs has a new test, the_dialog_scrolls_a_table_down_to_its_last_row, after the_dialog_opens_at_the_line_a_contents_search_found, and now imports `point` from gpui_kit. It opens the dialog with Space on a selected archive in the list view.
- image-preview-details, thumbnail-memory, choose-nu-path, get-info-stop-walk, search-settings-hints-steppers: no arm in common. The table arm of `preview_body` gained one line with a comment, and its footer an ID; expect at most a textual conflict there. The new tests in tests/basics.rs stand after a_table_preview_starts_at_its_left_edge_however_far_the_last_one_was_scrolled.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: a table kept selected across a view switch is drawn on another surface, with a new state, so it starts at its top there.
- Anyone who needs a picture of something scrolled: table-preview-scroll-add-scroll-steps.py (see left_out).

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change, outside this brief).
- A two-column table is at least 300 points wide (`width` in the table arm), and the Preview Pane at its default width leaves it 245 and the column view's card 270. So every archive's table there is wider than its card by 55 or 30 points. Short sizes still show, but the table scrolls sideways by that little, and, now that it scrolls down too, shows the horizontal thumb over its bottom row while scrolling. Letting the columns share the card's width when there are one or two of them would end both. Worth a brief.
- Column view: a sideways swipe over a table in the card moves the table and the columns together (the implementer's probe: a delta of -10 moved the columns 10 and the table 20 on screen; the same with the change reversed). The table's area doesn't stop a sideways event and the columns' plain overflow_x_scroll takes it as well.
- The line under a table is cut at the card's edge without an ellipsis when it is long: "Opened with Nushell · 300 rows, the first 200 shown" ends at "the first 20" in the Preview Pane (sheet -review-sheet-pane-2.png).
- A CSV that isn't text to the preview, a NUL byte in its first 8 KB is enough, is opened with Nushell and shown as a table, where every other CSV is shown as colored text. That is how load_preview is written (structured files that aren't text go to Nushell); it surprised me, and it is how I made a table of 12 columns.
- From the implementer, with the nu 0.116.0 installed here: `open x.msgpack` and `from msgpack` return binary (I saw the same), so the preview is a one-column table of the file's bytes, while the manual lists MessagePack among the files shown as tables; and an .xlsx shows one row per sheet, which the manual says only of databases. Whether a stock Nushell does the same I could not tell here.
